documents.title: Supporting evidence
documents.text:
I have worked for three years in a care home in Leeds; I started in October 2023. For me dignity means knocking before entering, explaining what I will do before personal care, and always closing curtains. I respect each person's culture and religion by asking what they want to eat, how they want to be treated, and whether they prefer being helped by a woman. One night I saw a bruise on a resident's arm, and I recorded it and told the nurse on duty immediately. In the dementia unit the residents were agitated at the end of the day, so we as a team moved dinner earlier.

I have moving and handling training and I use the hoist when supporting residents to move. I have medication training and I do the morning medication round for 18 residents. Before each shift I read each resident's care plan and do what is there. At the end of the shift I write daily notes in English and sign the medication sheet.

We always work in pairs. I made cards with food photos so each person can point to what they want to eat. I did two years of night shifts, and in the last year I moved to days.
